description: Nebula Works is a space-tech initiative exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, computer vision, interactive simulations, and space exploration. We are passionate about building creative, immersive solutions that make complex space concepts engaging and accessible. Our interests include AI/ML, software development, game design, and interactive technologies.
summary:
COSMIC LABS — Mission Architect is an interactive educational space mission design game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 by Team NebulaWorks. It allows players to become mission architects by selecting destinations such as Mars, the Moon, and asteroids, configuring mission objectives, and assembling spacecraft using modular components.

Players can explore a 3D spacecraft preview, evaluate engineering feasibility through mass, power, battery, communication, propulsion, and budget calculations, and receive educational guidance from the NEBULA advisor. They can then launch a deterministic mission simulation, make resource-management decisions, and review their mission outcomes through a debrief.

By transforming spacecraft design concepts into an interactive experience, COSMIC LABS makes space exploration more accessible and engaging. It encourages students and space enthusiasts to develop engineering thinking, problem-solving skills, and curiosity about aerospace technology.
details:
COSMIC LABS — Mission Architect

Team: NebulaWorks

1. What does the project do?

COSMIC LABS is an interactive educational space mission design game that allows users to experience the process of planning and evaluating a spacecraft mission.

Players begin by selecting an exploration destination: Mars, the Moon, or an asteroid. They configure their mission by specifying its name, objective, duration, budget, and difficulty. Next, they assemble a spacecraft by selecting modules from a centralized component library and explore their design through an interactive 3D preview.

The platform evaluates the spacecraft using a deterministic engineering feasibility engine. It calculates total mass, power generation and consumption, battery capacity, communication readiness, propulsion requirements, and estimated cost. Based on these results, users can understand design limitations and make improvements.

Once ready, players launch a staged mission simulation, encounter resource-management decisions, and review their performance through a mission debrief. The NEBULA educational advisor provides rule-based guidance to help users understand engineering concepts and feasibility warnings.

2. Benefits and intended impact

Spacecraft engineering involves multiple interconnected systems, making it challenging for beginners to understand how individual design decisions affect an entire mission.

COSMIC LABS addresses this challenge by transforming theoretical concepts into an interactive learning experience.

Its intended benefits include:

  • Making spacecraft systems and mission planning easier to understand.
  • Demonstrating engineering trade-offs involving mass, power, energy, communication, propulsion, and budget.
  • Encouraging experimentation, critical thinking, and problem-solving.
  • Helping students explore aerospace engineering through interactive gameplay.
  • Making space exploration concepts more accessible to students and space enthusiasts.

Our goal is to inspire curiosity about space science and encourage more learners to explore aerospace technology.

3. Technology and tools used

We developed COSMIC LABS using the following technologies:

  • Next.js App Router: Application framework and routing.
  • React: Interactive user interface.
  • TypeScript: Type-safe application development.
  • Zustand: State management and browser persistence.
  • Three.js: 3D graphics and visualization.
  • React Three Fiber: Integration of 3D scenes with React.
  • Drei: Utilities for interactive 3D rendering.
  • MediaPipe Tasks Vision: Optional hand-landmark and gesture recognition.
  • Framer Motion: UI animations and transitions.
  • Custom CSS: Space-inspired visual design system.

The NEBULA advisor uses a server-side rule-based approach, allowing educational guidance without requiring an external AI API key.

The project uses browser-based software and webcam access for optional gesture recognition. No dedicated GPU or specialized hardware is required.

4. What makes the project creative?

COSMIC LABS combines elements of a spacecraft engineering workstation, an educational simulation, and an interactive game.

Instead of simply presenting information about spacecraft components, it allows users to assemble a spacecraft, inspect its engineering parameters, evaluate its readiness, and experience the consequences of mission decisions.

Its distinctive elements include:

  • A modular 3D spacecraft visualization experience.
  • Optional computer vision-based hand gesture recognition.
  • A deterministic engineering feasibility engine.
  • Mission simulations with resource-management decisions.
  • NEBULA, a local educational mission advisor.
  • A mission debrief that connects engineering decisions with mission outcomes.

The combination of these features creates an engaging environment where learning happens through experimentation.

5. Engineering factors and design considerations

During development, we considered several factors to keep the application accessible, reliable, and technically understandable:

  • Engineering constraints: Mass, power, battery capacity, communication, propulsion, and budget must be evaluated together.
  • Scientific responsibility: The application uses simplified fictional educational parameters rather than claiming to reproduce real NASA spacecraft specifications.
  • Reliability: Engineering calculations and mission outcomes are deterministic, making results consistent and understandable.
  • Accessibility: Mouse and keyboard interaction remain available even when webcam-based gesture recognition is unavailable.
  • Privacy: Camera access is requested only after the user explicitly enables the feature.
  • Performance: The application uses modular components and browser-based rendering.
  • Maintainability: Mission data, component definitions, engineering calculations, application state, and UI components are separated into dedicated modules.

6. NASA educational connection

We consulted official NASA educational resources to inform the learning experience, including:

  • NASA State-of-the-Art Small Spacecraft Technology.
  • NASA JPL — Build a Satellite.
  • NASA Science — Basics of Space Flight.
  • NASA JPL — Design Your Spacecraft.

These resources are accessible through the in-app Science Desk, connecting users with further learning material about spacecraft systems and mission design.

COSMIC LABS uses NASA educational resources for reference and learning. It does not claim to use NASA datasets or represent an official NASA engineering simulator.

7. Our vision

With COSMIC LABS, we want to make space mission design an experience that anyone curious about space can explore.

We believe that learning becomes more meaningful when people can build, experiment, make decisions, and discover the results for themselves.

COSMIC LABS — Build. Engineer. Launch. Discover.
